root_idea.summary: The root has two documented semantic axes: movement or agitation, and benefit, giving, or nourishment.
root_idea.development: The movement axis develops through shaking, swaying, convulsion, inclination, and dizziness. The benefactive axis extends through giving and supplying food to the food-laden table designated by مَائِدَةٌ.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form مَادَ rather than the Quranic imperfect تَمِيدَ.
Displayed as the normalized nominal citation form مَائِدَةٌ.

senses.definition: To move, sway, or convulse violently.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrences, the earth is the subject and the construction with بِـ describes its convulsive movement affecting people: أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ and أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ.

senses.definition: A table spread or laid with food; a food-laden table.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrences, the word denotes the heavenly table spread with food.

senses.definition: The nourishment requested from heaven, figuratively understood as knowledge that nourishes the hearts.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a reported Quran-focused interpretation of the heavenly-table request, especially the passage in 5:114; it is a figurative extension rather than the ordinary physical definition of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn or twist about, becoming contorted or convulsed.
To writhe upon a spear after being pierced.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional construction describing the contortions of a wounded person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To quiver or tremble, as a mirage.
To become confounded, perplexed, or amazed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded as a figurative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To experience heaving of the stomach, a tendency to vomit, and dizziness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or physical use associated with intoxication or travel by sea.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to reel or be carried round through the motion of the sea or ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in constructions such as مَادَ بِهِ الْبَحْرُ and مَادَتْ بِهِ الْأَرْضُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become altered in odor, or become stinking, through dew or moisture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded of the colocynth and, similarly, a date.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incline or sway from side to side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded of branches, a person's gait, and an earth described as inclining; the human-gait use can convey affected elegance, pride, or self-conceit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bestow a benefit, favor, or gift; to give.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be a person receiving the benefit or gift.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To furnish travelers with provisions or bring people wheat or food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The provisioning use is compared with زَادَ; bringing wheat or food is also recorded as a dialectal equivalent of مَارَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To trade as a merchant.
To increase or grow.
To ask or desire someone to give something, especially wheat or food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The food-related use is a specific application of the construction of seeking something from another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dialectal particle meaning other than or except, on or upon, or because of.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is recorded as a dialectal form of بَيْدَ with several particle functions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: On account of that; for the sake of that.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the fixed expression فَعَلْتُهُ مَيْدَا ذَلِكَ or مَيْدَ ذَلِكَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The amount, measure, dimensions, or extent of a thing; also the surface or extent of a road and the furthest distance to which horses run.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can refer to the measure of a thing's sides or its spatial limit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mode, manner, or fashion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing things constructed according to one mode.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Opposite to or facing something; directly across from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of one house or place in relation to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse-course, race-ground, or hippodrome.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is مَيَادِينُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A delicate, pleasant, ample, or easy life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression عَيْشٌ مَيْدَانٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A historical term for the period of a caliph's reign, given as roughly twenty to twenty-four years.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in مَيْدَانُ الْخُلَفَاءِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Much moving, agitated, or vacillating.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive epithet also applied figuratively to worldly prosperity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Affected by heaving of the stomach, a tendency to vomit, and dizziness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Associated with intoxication or voyaging upon the sea.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Inclining or swaying from side to side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded of a branch and of a person whose affected gait conveys elegance, pride, or self-conceit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: By metonymy, the table itself even without food, or the food itself even without a table.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The table-alone extension is reported with disagreement among authorities; the food-alone extension is also recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A round piece of ground or land, by comparison with a table.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Calamities.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded as a transposed form related to مَآوِدُ, distinct from the ordinary plural of مَائِدَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who asks or desires a gift, or one from whom a gift is requested; also one asking to bring wheat or food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry records both participant-role readings of the gift-seeking relation, with the food-related use as a specific application.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Being made to reel by sea or ground.
Moisture-induced alteration in plants or dates.
Intensive epithet for movement or vacillation.
Calamities as a reported transposed form.

cautions: The Quranic verb is displayed under the perfect citation form مَادَ, while all supplied Quran occurrences are the imperfect تَمِيدَ.
The knowledge reading of مَائِدَةٌ is explicitly reported as a figurative interpretation of the heavenly-table passage, not as its ordinary physical gloss.
